name: Ingress: host + path routing
objective: CKA › Services & Networking. An Ingress is L7 HTTP routing rules (host + path → Service:port) realized by an ingress controller via an IngressClass. Create a host rule to one Service, then add path-based routing to a second. Graded on the Ingress spec (this bench has no ingress controller; the object is what the exam checks).

questions.title: Route a host to a Service
questions.teach:
An **Ingress** maps HTTP `host` + `path` to a backend `Service:port`. `spec.ingressClassName` picks which controller implements it. A `pathType` of `Prefix` matches by path prefix; `Exact` matches the whole path.

**Gotcha:** Ingress routes to a **Service**, not pods directly — the Service must exist and have endpoints. `kubectl create ingress` is the fast path: `--rule='host/path=svc:port'`.
questions.prompt:
The Services `web` and `api` (both port 80) already exist in `ingress-learn`. Create an Ingress `shop` (ingressClassName `nginx`) that routes host `shop.example.com` path `/` (pathType `Prefix`) to Service `web:80`.

Target: Ingress `shop` has ingressClassName `nginx` and a rule host=shop.example.com, path `/` Prefix → web:80.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ingress-learn create ingress shop --class=nginx --rule='shop.example.com/*=web:80'` (the `/*` gives pathType Prefix). Or write the YAML with `pathType: Prefix` and `backend.service.name: web`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: shop, namespace: ingress-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: web
            port:
              number: 80
YAML

verification.description: Ingress shop: class nginx, host shop.example.com path / Prefix -> web:80

questions.eli5:
Imagine a big office building with one front receptionist (the ingress controller). Visitors arrive asking for a company by name — *"I'm here for shop.example.com."* The receptionist checks a **directory sheet** that says which floor/desk (which Service) handles each company name and web path. That directory sheet is the **Ingress**.

Your sheet entry says: *"Anyone asking for host `shop.example.com`, any path starting with `/`, send them to the `web` desk on port 80."* The receptionist does the walking; your job is just to write the directory entry.

- **`ingressClassName: nginx`** tells which receptionist reads this sheet (a building can have several).
- **`host`** is the company name the visitor typed.
- **`pathType: Prefix`** with path `/` means *"any path that starts with /"* — basically everything.
- **The backend is a Service, never a pod** — the receptionist forwards to a desk (Service), and that desk routes to whoever's working (the pods behind it).

**Watch out for:**

- **Ingress points to a Service, not pods directly.** The Service `web` must exist and have healthy endpoints, or traffic goes nowhere.
- **`pathType` is required** — the common values are `Prefix` (match by path prefix) and `Exact` (match the whole path exactly). The handy `kubectl create ingress ... --rule='host/*=svc:80'` sets `Prefix` for you; `host/path` (no `*`) sets `Exact`.
- **`ingressClassName` must match a real controller.** Name the wrong class and no controller picks it up.
- **The port is the Service's port (80 here), not a pod port.**
- **This bench has no ingress controller**, so nothing actually serves traffic — grading checks the **Ingress object/spec**, exactly like the real exam.
questions.deepDive:
## Ingress: host → Service — full rundown

### Mental model
An **Ingress** is a set of **L7 (HTTP/HTTPS) routing rules**: `host` + `path` → `Service:port`. It is only *data*; a running **ingress controller** (nginx, traefik, etc.), selected via **`ingressClassName`**, reads the object and actually proxies traffic. No controller → the object exists but nothing routes.

> Ingress = the routing table. The controller = the proxy that enforces it. The Service = the real backend.

### Imperative create (fast path)
```bash
kubectl -n ingress-learn create ingress shop \
  --class=nginx \
  --rule='shop.example.com/*=web:80'
#          └ host ┘ └path┘  └svc:port┘
```
- Trailing **`/*`** → `pathType: Prefix`.
- A plain **`/path`** (no `*`) → `pathType: Exact`.
- Multiple `--rule=` flags add more host/path entries.

### Declarative manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shop
  namespace: ingress-learn
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx          # which controller implements this
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com         # L7 host header match
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix           # Prefix | Exact | ImplementationSpecific
        backend:
          service:
            name: web              # a Service, must exist + have endpoints
            port:
              number: 80           # Service port (name: also allowed)
```

### pathType
| pathType | Matches |
|---|---|
| `Prefix` | Path treated as `/`-split segments; `/` matches everything, `/api` matches `/api` and `/api/...` (not `/apifoo`). |
| `Exact` | The entire URL path must equal the value, case-sensitive. |
| `ImplementationSpecific` | Delegated to the controller's own matching. |

**`pathType` is mandatory** on every path in `networking.k8s.io/v1`.

### Key fields
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `spec.ingressClassName` | Names the `IngressClass`/controller. Replaces the old `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation. |
| `spec.rules[].host` | Virtual host; omit to match all hosts. |
| `spec.rules[].http.paths[].path` | URL path to match. |
| `backend.service.name` / `port.number` | Target **Service** and its port (not a pod). |
| `spec.defaultBackend` | Catch-all for unmatched requests (optional). |
| `spec.tls[]` | Hosts + Secret for HTTPS termination (optional). |

### Inspect
```bash
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress
kubectl -n ingress-learn describe ingress shop
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress shop -o yaml
kubectl get ingressclass                 # which classes exist
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Backend is a Service, not pods.** The `web` Service must exist and have **endpoints**, or requests 404/502 even with a perfect Ingress.
- **`pathType` is required** — forgetting it makes `kubectl apply` reject the manifest.
- **`ingressClassName` must match a deployed controller.** Wrong/missing class → nothing routes.
- **Prefix `/` catches everything**; be careful ordering vs. more specific paths (longest match wins at request time, not manifest order).
- **`v1` structure changed**: `backend.service.name` / `backend.service.port.number`, not the old `serviceName`/`servicePort`.
- **No controller on this bench** → object is graded, traffic is not. Same as the exam's object checks.
- A **host with no matching path** falls through to `defaultBackend` if set, else 404.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n ingress-learn create ingress shop \
  --class=nginx --rule='shop.example.com/*=web:80'
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress shop -o yaml   # verify host/path/backend
```

questions.title: Add path-based routing
questions.teach:
A single host can fan out by path: add another path entry under the same host routing to a different Service. The controller matches the most specific path first.

**Gotcha:** `Prefix` `/api` matches `/api` and `/api/...`; ordering in the manifest doesn't decide precedence — longest-matching path wins at request time.
questions.prompt:
Extend Ingress `shop`: under host `shop.example.com`, add path `/api` (pathType `Prefix`) routing to Service `api:80` (keep the `/` → web:80 rule).

Target: Ingress `shop` has both paths under shop.example.com — `/` → web:80 and `/api` → api:80.
questions.hint: Edit the Ingress and add a second `paths` entry: `path: /api, pathType: Prefix, backend.service.name: api, port 80`. `kubectl -n ingress-learn edit ingress shop` or re-apply the full YAML with both paths.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: shop, namespace: ingress-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: web, port: { number: 80 } } }
      - path: /api
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: api, port: { number: 80 } } }
YAML

verification.description: Ingress shop has /api Prefix -> api:80 alongside / -> web:80

questions.eli5:
Same office building, same receptionist, same company (`shop.example.com`). But now the company has **two departments** and you want visitors routed by the **web path** they ask for:

- Ask for `/` (or anything starting with it) → go to the **`web`** desk.
- Ask for `/api` (or `/api/...`) → go to the **`api`** desk.

So you add a **second line** to the same directory entry for that host. The receptionist reads the request path and sends each visitor to the right desk. This is **path-based fan-out**: one hostname, many backends, split by URL path.

The important twist: when two paths could both match (e.g. `/` and `/api` both "start with /"), the receptionist uses the **most specific (longest) match**. So `/api/orders` goes to the `api` desk because `/api` is a longer match than `/`. **The order you list them in the file doesn't decide this** — longest-matching path wins at request time.

**Watch out for:**

- **Keep the existing `/` → web rule** — you're *adding* a path, not replacing. The target requires **both** paths present.
- **Precedence is by longest path match, not manifest order.** Listing `/` first doesn't make it win over `/api`.
- **`Prefix /api`** matches `/api` and `/api/anything`, but **not** `/apifoo` — prefix matching is on whole path segments.
- **Each path still needs its own `pathType`** and its own Service backend (`api` must exist with endpoints).
- **Both paths live under the same `host` block** (`shop.example.com`), as separate entries in the `paths` list — not two separate rules unless you want different hosts.
- **No ingress controller on this bench** — grading is on the Ingress spec, like the exam.
questions.deepDive:
## Ingress: path-based fan-out — full rundown

### Mental model
A single `host` can route to **multiple Services** by URL **path**. You add more entries to that host's `paths` list, each with its own `pathType` and `backend`. At request time the controller picks the **longest matching path** — manifest order is irrelevant.

> One hostname, many backends, split by path. Specificity (longest prefix) decides, not list order.

### Full manifest (both paths)
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shop
  namespace: ingress-learn
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /                    # keep the original
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service: { name: web, port: { number: 80 } }
      - path: /api                 # the new, more specific route
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service: { name: api, port: { number: 80 } }
```

### Editing in place
```bash
kubectl -n ingress-learn edit ingress shop     # add the /api paths entry
# or re-apply the full YAML (declarative, idempotent) — preferred
```
> `kubectl create ingress --rule=` creates a *new* object; to extend an existing one, `edit` or re-`apply` the complete spec.

### Path matching & precedence
| Request | `/` (Prefix) | `/api` (Prefix) | Winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | match | — | `web` |
| `/images/logo.png` | match | — | `web` |
| `/api` | match | match | **`api`** (longer) |
| `/api/orders` | match | match | **`api`** (longer) |
| `/apifoo` | match | — (not a segment boundary) | `web` |

- **Prefix** matches on whole path **segments**: `/api` matches `/api` and `/api/...` but **not** `/apifoo`.
- **Longest matching path wins** regardless of order in the manifest.
- Use **`Exact`** when you need `/api` to match *only* `/api` and nothing deeper.

### Multiple hosts vs multiple paths
```yaml
rules:
- host: shop.example.com      # path fan-out under ONE host
  http: { paths: [ {path: /, ...}, {path: /api, ...} ] }
- host: admin.example.com     # a DIFFERENT host = another rule entry
  http: { paths: [ {path: /, ...} ] }
```
Different **paths** → more entries in the same `paths` list. Different **hosts** → more entries in `rules`.

### Inspect
```bash
kubectl -n ingress-learn describe ingress shop
#   Rules:
#     Host              Path   Backends
#     shop.example.com  /      web:80 (...)
#                       /api   api:80 (...)
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress shop -o yaml
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Don't drop the existing route.** Extending = add a path, keep `/` → web. Re-applying must include **both** entries.
- **Order ≠ precedence.** Listing `/` before `/api` doesn't make `/` win; the **longest** match does.
- **`Prefix /api` won't catch `/apifoo`** — segment-boundary matching. Use `Exact` for strict single-path matches.
- **Each path needs its own `pathType`** (required) and a backend Service that **exists with endpoints**.
- **Same host → one `rules[]` entry with many `paths`**; a new host → a new `rules[]` entry.
- **`v1` backend shape**: `backend.service.name` + `backend.service.port.number`.
- **No controller here** → the **spec is graded**, not live routing (mirrors the exam).

### Quick reference
```yaml
paths:
- { path: /,    pathType: Prefix, backend: { service: { name: web, port: { number: 80 } } } }
- { path: /api, pathType: Prefix, backend: { service: { name: api, port: { number: 80 } } } }
```
```bash
kubectl -n ingress-learn get ingress shop -o yaml   # confirm BOTH paths present
```
